title: CI3 Sessions — Making the Site Remember You
description: Store the logged-in username in a CI3 session and read it back on a separate request.
objectives: Store a submitted value in the session with set_userdata
Read that value back on a separate request with userdata
Explain the error a missing library load produces
Apply sess_destroy to clear a session at logout
recap: set_userdata puts a value in the session box under a key you pick.
userdata reads it back from any method, form or no form.
Without the library load, $this->session does not exist in that method.
sess_destroy empties the box, so userdata returns NULL again.

chunks.text: A session is a small box of values the server keeps for one browser. Before you touch it, load it: $this->load->library('session');

check.question: What must happen before you use $this->session?
options: Load the session library
Open the login form again

chunks.text: $this->session->set_userdata('username', $username); puts a value in the box under a name you pick.

check.question: What is 'username' in that line?
options: The name of the value in the box
The password typed in the form

chunks.text: login() shows the form with $this->load->view('login_form');, then check() reads it with $this->input->post('username'); and stores it.

check.question: Which method stores the name in the session?
options: check()
login()

quiz.question: What does the third line actually do?
options: Prints the typed username back onto the page
Saves the typed name in the box under 'username'
Checks the typed name against the users table
Sends the typed name back to the login form file to be shown

chunks.text: $this->session->userdata('username') gets the value back. It returns NULL when nothing is stored.

check.question: What comes back when nothing was stored?
options: NULL
An empty form

chunks.text: home() is a separate request. No form data reaches it at all, yet it can still read the box.

check.question: Does home() need the form to get the name?
options: No, it reads the session
Yes, it reads the post

chunks.text: var_dump shows type and length, so string(5) "maria" looks different from NULL on screen.

check.question: Why var_dump instead of echo here?
options: It shows a missing value clearly
It runs faster than echo does

quiz.question: Type the value userdata gives back after these two lines run.

chunks.text: Every method that touches $this->session must load the library first. There is no shortcut.

check.question: How many methods need the load line?
options: Every one that uses the session
Only the very first one to run

chunks.text: Drop that line from home() and PHP says Undefined property: Auth::$session.

check.question: What does that message mean?
options: $this->session was never made
The stored name was deleted

chunks.text: The stored value is untouched. Only that one method cannot reach it.

check.question: Does the error erase the saved name?
options: No, the box is still filled
Yes, the box is emptied out

quiz.question: Arrange the tokens into a working home() body.

chunks.text: $this->session->sess_destroy(); empties the box. It takes no arguments and it cannot be undone.

check.question: What does sess_destroy() need passed in?
options: Nothing at all
The key to remove

chunks.text: logout() loads the library, then destroys — the same first line as check() and home().

check.question: Can logout() skip the load line?
options: No, it uses the session
Yes, check() loaded it

chunks.text: After logout, userdata('username') gives NULL again, exactly like before anyone logged in.

check.question: What does home() show after logout?
options: NULL
The last name saved

quiz.question: A teammate stored 'email' in check(), never logged out, then opened home() in a new tab. What prints?
options: NULL, because a new tab starts a brand new session box
The stored email, since the box is still filled
NULL, because only post data survives between requests
The stored email, but only until the page is refreshed
